meta.disclaimer: Reference information compiled from official government sources. Not legal or tax advice. Check the cited source before relying on any value.

facts.value: no later than the next business day after discharge
facts.summary: Connecticut: when an employee is fired or laid off, final wages are due no later than the next business day after discharge.
facts.evidence_quote: (b) Whenever an employer discharges an Employee, the employer shall pay the employee's wages in full no later than the business day next succeeding the date of such discharge.
facts.source_title: Connecticut Wage Payment Laws (CT DOL compilation, Conn. Gen. Stat. 31-71c)
facts.notes: Laid-off employees: not later than the next regular payday (31-71c(c)).

facts.value: not later than the next regular payday
facts.summary: Connecticut: when an employee is quits or resigns, final wages are due not later than the next regular payday.
facts.evidence_quote: (a) Whenever an employee voluntarily terminates his employment, the employer shall pay the employee's wages in full not later than the next regular pay day
facts.source_title: Connecticut Wage Payment Laws (CT DOL compilation, Conn. Gen. Stat. 31-71c)

facts.applies_to: As listed by U.S. DOL, page updated November 5, 2026
facts.summary: Connecticut basic state minimum wage listed by U.S. DOL: $16.94.
facts.evidence_quote: Basic Minimum Rate (per hour): $16.94 Premium Pay After Designated Hours 1 : Weekly - 40 In restaurants and hotel restaurants, for the 7th consecutive day of work, premium pay is required at time and one half the minimum rate.
facts.source_title: State Minimum Wage Laws (U.S. DOL Wage and Hour Division)
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Wage and Hour Division
facts.notes: Local (city or county) minimum wages are not included. Scheduled January 1, 2027 increases are not reflected until DOL updates the page.

facts.value: Yes. Report independent contractors if remuneration for services is anticipated to exceed $5,000/year.
facts.summary: Connecticut independent contractor reporting required? (per OCSE): Yes. Report independent contractors if remuneration for services is anticipated to exceed $5,000/year.
facts.evidence_quote: Independent Contractor Reporting Required?: Yes. Report independent contractors if remuneration for services is anticipated to exceed $5,000/year.
facts.source_title: State New Hire Reporting, State Contact and Program Information (HHS OCSE Intergovernmental Reference Guide)
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, Office of Child Support Services
facts.notes: Text as entered by the state in the OCSE guide.

facts.summary: Connecticut new hire reporting timeframe (per OCSE): Within 20 days of hire date
facts.evidence_quote: Reporting Timeframe: Within 20 days of hire date
facts.source_title: State New Hire Reporting, State Contact and Program Information (HHS OCSE Intergovernmental Reference Guide)
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, Office of Child Support Services
facts.notes: Federal floor is 20 days; states may set shorter deadlines. Text as entered by the state in the OCSE guide.

facts.summary: Connecticut: frequencies marked in the U.S. DOL State Payday Requirements table: Weekly (note 4).
facts.source_title: State Payday Requirements (U.S. DOL Wage and Hour Division)
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Wage and Hour Division
facts.notes: Note 4: Connecticut. Longer intervals (up to monthly) are permitted if approved by the labor commissioner. | DOL table last revised 2023-01-01; DOL says to consult the state labor office for official information. Confirm against current state law before relying on it.

facts.summary: Connecticut is not listed with a final 2026 FUTA credit reduction, so the effective FUTA rate is 0.6% on the first $7,000 per employee (if the full 5.4% state credit applies).
facts.evidence_quote: State not listed in the Final 2026 FUTA Credit Reductions table.
facts.source_title: Final 2026 Federal Unemployment Tax Act (FUTA) Credit Reductions (updated November 10, 2026)
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Employment and Training Administration
